Sample includes 64 healthy adults (mean age 21.2, range 18–26), meeting the age and health criteria. Whole-brain results are clearly described and thresholded, satisfying reporting requirements. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion, and no exclusion criteria apply. Therefore all inclusion criteria (I3, I4, I5, I6) are met.

This is an empirical fMRI study in healthy adults that investigates social gaze effects on action control using a task involving face (social) vs object (nonsocial) stimuli. Sample: 23 healthy right-handed adults aged 21–37, satisfying the adult age criterion. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked analyses (SPM5 second-level random-effects ANOVA; main effects and interactions reported; cluster-level corrected maps and a table of neural correlates are provided), satisfying whole-brain evidence requirements. The task is explicitly social-related (social gaze, social communication/perception). Full article content (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is present. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only contrasts, out-of-range ages, or non-empirical) are met.

This is an fMRI study using a social task (Cyberball social exclusion), includes a healthy adult participant group (16 adult female participants), and reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task activation results (exclusion>inclusion main effects reported with cluster-level FWE correction and tables of peak coordinates). Whole-brain analyses and coordinates are clearly described in the text and tables. Therefore the paper meets inclusion criteria I3 (social fMRI task), I4 (healthy adult sample present), I5 (group-level whole-brain task-evoked maps reported), and I6 (results reported as coordinates/tables). No exclusion criteria (E2–E6) apply. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion present).

This article reports task-based fMRI in healthy adult participants (n=98, mean age 20.7) during social judgments about self, friends, and strangers—directly addressing social cognition (Perception and Understanding of Self/Others). The full text contains Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion and reports group-level whole-brain task contrasts (e.g., self > Bush, friends > strangers) presented in figures and described in the text (thresholded whole-brain maps reported at p<0.001 uncorrected). Thus it meets inclusion criteria I3 (social fMRI task), I4 (healthy adult sample 18–65), I5 (group-level whole-brain task-evoked maps), and I6 (whole-brain results clearly described/figured). No exclusion criteria (E2–E6) are triggered. Full text appears complete.

This is an fMRI study of social processes (empathy/sympathy) in a healthy sample (ages 7–40) and reports whole-brain task-evoked results for the combined sample. However, the meta-analysis requires at least one group-level, whole-brain map clearly identified as coming from a healthy adult group (age 18–65). This paper does not report an adult-only group-level whole-brain activation map or otherwise separate adult-only results; all primary whole-brain contrasts are reported for the mixed-age (7–40) cohort and age-correlations. Therefore it does not meet inclusion criteria I4 and I5 for an adult-specific healthy group whole-brain task effect. I apply exclusion criterion E4 (no unmasked whole-brain healthy-adult group task map reported). Inclusion criteria met: I3 (fMRI during social-related task) and I6 (whole-brain results reported in standard formats). Inclusion criteria not met: I4 (adult-only healthy group results not separately reported) and I5 (no whole-brain map clearly identified as from a healthy adult group).

Full text provided appears to be abstract and references only (no full methods/results). The study sampled adolescents (three phases of adolescence) rather than adults. Inclusion: I3 (uses fMRI during a social task - Trust Game) is satisfied. Inclusion I4 (healthy adults 18-65) is not met. Inclusion I5 (reports group-level whole-brain voxelwise healthy-group task maps) cannot be confirmed from the provided abstract. Exclusion E5 (participants outside age range with no separate adult subgroup) is met. Because the full text is incomplete, exclusion is based on adolescent-only sample and inability to verify adult whole-brain results.

This is an empirical fMRI study of face individuation, a form of ‘Perception and Understanding of Others’ (social-related processing). The sample comprises healthy adults (final N=15; mean age 24.8). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses of task-evoked activation (whole-brain individuation contrasts with cluster correction; supplementary whole-brain maps/tables are described). Full article text (intro, methods, results, discussion, whole-brain results) is provided. Thus it satisfies I3 (social-related fMRI task), I4 (healthy adult sample 18–65), I5 (group-level whole-brain task-evoked maps), and I6 (whole-brain results clearly described and presented). No exclusion criteria are met. Full text appears complete.

The manuscript reports an event-related fMRI task explicitly probing social perception/understanding (categorization of social interaction vs non-social point-light displays), uses a healthy adult sample (N=14, mean age 29.4), and provides group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses (one-sample random-effects t-test with FDR-corrected maps, cluster tables and figures). The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion, and therefore is complete for screening. It meets inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, and I6 and does not violate any exclusion criteria (E2–E6).

This is an empirical fMRI study of humor (a social-related process) in healthy adults (n=29, mean age 27). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain task-evoked contrasts (Cartoons vs Neutral) and parametric modulation analyses, with conjunctions, direct contrasts, and tables/figures of peak coordinates and cluster-corrected results. These satisfy the meta-analysis inclusion criteria for social-related fMRI tasks, healthy adult sample, and whole-brain reporting. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, age outside range, non-empirical) apply. Full text contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion (complete).

The paper reports an event-related functional MRI study of social expectation violations (forming impressions of politicians with congruent/incongruent political views), which is a social-related task. Participants are healthy adults (N=18 analyzed, ages 19–30). The manuscript reports group-level, whole-brain random-effects analyses (second-level one-sample t-tests) with voxelwise results surviving FDR correction, and provides a table of coordinates and figures describing the activations (i.e., unmasked healthy-group task contrasts). ROI analyses are also presented, but whole-brain task-evoked maps are clearly reported. The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. Therefore inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5 and I6 are satisfied and no exclusion criteria apply.

This is an fMRI study of social-related processing in healthy adults. The task manipulated social vs. non-social contexts during encoding and measured recognition in an fMRI retrieval task, addressing social interaction and social-context representation (I3). The sample comprises 24 healthy adults aged 18–28, satisfying the adult sample requirement (I4). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses (SPM5 random-effects model) with contrasts and tables/figures of activations (e.g., Table 3, Figs. 3–5), meeting the whole-brain evidence requirement (I5,I6). The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion; fulltext appears complete. No exclusion criteria apply.

Full text is incomplete (only abstract/metadata available). From available content: I3 (fMRI during social-related task) and I4 (healthy adult sample 20 young adults within 18–65) appear satisfied. However, I5 (reporting of at least one group-level whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked statistical map for the healthy group) cannot be confirmed from the abstract/metadata because the PDF full text and results/tables/figures are not accessible. I6 (acceptability of whole-brain results reported in tables/figures/supplement) cannot be verified. No exclusion criteria (E2–E6) are clearly met based on available information. Because a required inclusion criterion (I5) cannot be verified and the full text is incomplete, the study is excluded pending access to the complete article.

This study reports task-based fMRI in healthy adult participants (n=22 males, mean age 24.2) performing social-related judgements (allocentric social hierarchy and social alliance). The paper presents group-level, whole-brain (random-effects second-level) task contrasts (e.g., social hierarchy vs. baselines; social alliance vs. number-equal) with voxelwise results reported at p<0.05 FWE and coordinates/tables/figures. Methods, results, and discussion are present in the full text. Thus all inclusion criteria are met (I3, I4, I5, I6) and no exclusion criteria apply. The full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion, tables/figures referenced).

This is an empirical fMRI study in healthy adults (N=25, mean age 20.2) that uses a social-related task (family assistance/prosocial decisions) during task-based fMRI. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain task contrasts (Costly-Donation versus Noncostly-Reward), tables of coordinates, and whole-brain and ROI-corrected results and PPI analyses; results are clearly described for the healthy sample. Full article text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is provided. Therefore it meets the review objective and inclusion criteria.

This is an fMRI study of self-face recognition (Perception and Understanding of Self), a social-related task. Participants: healthy adults (n=16 analyzed), ages 19–24, meeting the sample criterion. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked analyses (SPM random-effects, reported clusters, coordinates, and thresholding) with results clearly attributed to the healthy group (e.g., MPFC, PCC, precuneus, FFA). Whole-brain results are reported in text/tables with coordinates. Full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion and appears complete. No exclusion criteria (E2–E6) are met.

This study reports an fMRI task involving observation of virtual social interactions (meets I3). Participants are described as healthy adults (data from 15 participants), meeting I4. Methods specify whole-brain EPI acquisition and SPM analysis, and the paper presents group-level activation maps (Figure and text describing voxelwise activations in STS, mPFC, amygdala) time-locked to task events, satisfying I5 and I6. No exclusion criteria (E2–E6) are met. Note: the provided full text appears truncated (methods and representative results present, but introduction/discussion not included), so fulltext_incomplete is set to true. Given available evidence, the study should be included, but confidence is reduced by the incomplete full text.

This is an fMRI study of social processing (eye contact and spontaneous mimicry), using a task tapping social communication/affiliation processes (meets I3). Sample comprises 20 healthy adult participants (mean age 23), reported separately (meets I4). The paper reports multiple group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task contrasts (e.g., Congruent > Catch, Incongruent > Catch, Direct > Averted, interaction contrasts) with thresholding and cluster-level FWE correction and coordinates in Table 1 and figures (meets I5 and I6). The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion (fulltext_incomplete=false). No exclusion criteria are met (e.g., not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not between-group-only, participants within age range, empirical fMRI data present). Therefore I recommend inclusion for the meta-analysis.

This is an empirical fMRI study of social cognition in healthy adults. The task involved social-comparative judgments (close other vs. non-close other) during fMRI; participants were healthy adults (mean age 18.7, right-handed, prescreened). The paper reports group-level, voxelwise second-level SPM contrasts (random-effects), provides peak coordinates and cluster statistics for task contrasts (e.g., Target × Breadth interaction, Valence contrasts, Close Other > Non-Close Other), and corrected statistical maps (FWE) and tables/figures for the healthy group. Full article text including Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion is provided. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, and I6 and violates no exclusion criteria.

Full text appears incomplete (only title/abstract/metadata provided). Abstract indicates an fMRI study of face-voice integration (social perception), so inclusion criterion I3 (social-related fMRI task) is likely met. However critical details are missing to confirm I4 (that participants are healthy adults aged 18–65) and I5 (reporting of a group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked map). I6 (acceptable reporting format) likewise cannot be confirmed. No explicit exclusion criteria from the provided list (E2–E6) are clearly met based on the abstract alone. Because the full text is not available to verify participant characteristics and whole-brain results, I exclude the study pending access to the complete article.

This is an empirical fMRI study in healthy adult participants (N=19, ages 19–28) who performed social-related tasks (categorical knowledge and feature verification including social-category trials). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain, random-effects voxelwise contrasts (e.g., ‘social > non-social’ and ‘non-social > social’) with corrected thresholds and tables/figures of peak coordinates, satisfying whole-brain reporting. Full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results and Discussion. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity/resting-only, not between-group-only, ages within 18–65, empirical data present).

This is an original, empirical fMRI study in healthy adults (N=24, ages 18–34) using a social-related task (emotion perception/integration of facial and vocal emotions). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task contrasts (e.g., (AV > A) ∩ (AV > V), CAV > ICAV) with FDR-corrected thresholds and coordinate tables/figures, satisfying whole-brain evidence requirements. It is not ROI-only, connectivity-only, nor between-group-only, and participants are within the 18–65 age range. Full article content (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is provided. Therefore all inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, and I6 are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

This is an fMRI study of social competition (human–human vs human–machine) using a task designed to elicit Theory of Mind and executive processes. Participants were healthy adults (n=14, mean age 35.9; results analyzed for healthy subjects). The paper reports whole-brain, group-level voxelwise analyses (SPM5 random-effects group contrasts, thresholds and Talairach/MNI coordinates, tables of activations) for main effects and interactions. Full article includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Therefore it meets the review’s requirements for task-based fMRI of social processing in healthy adults and reports whole-brain healthy-group task activation maps. No exclusion criteria are met.

This is an empirical fMRI study of social processing: participants played Cyberball (a social exclusion paradigm) during fMRI, satisfying the social-related task requirement. The sample consists of healthy adults (n=20 after exclusions; mean age ~25), within the 18–65 range. The paper reports whole-brain group-level task contrasts (social exclusion > fair play) with cluster-corrected maps, tables of coordinates, and figures—meeting whole-brain evidence and acceptable reporting formats. The full text provided includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion, so full text is complete. Therefore all inclusion criteria (I3, I4, I5, I6) are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

This is an empirical fMRI study of social decision-making (ultimatum game), using real-time and offline fMRI analyses to predict accept/reject decisions. Sample: healthy adult participants (male, ages 23–28) reported separately. The paper reports whole-brain offline analyses with discriminating volumes, MNI coordinates, and thresholded voxelwise results (tables/figures), satisfying whole-brain evidence requirements. Full text includes methods, results, and discussion. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, includes healthy adults, not a review).

This is an empirical fMRI study in healthy adult participants (13 right-handed males, mean age 28.2) that uses a social-related task (perception of biological motion, a measure of perception/understanding of others). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain, voxelwise task activation maps (canonical vs scrambled biological motion) with corrected thresholds and provides MNI coordinates and tables. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I3 (social-related fMRI task), I4 (healthy adult sample 18–65), I5 (group-level whole-brain task-evoked map reported), and I6 (results reported as coordinates/tables/figures). No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not exclusive connectivity-only, not between-group-only, age appropriate, and empirical). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion present).

This fMRI study investigates affective (social) touch processing—an explicitly social-related task—using whole-brain, group-level voxelwise analyses in a sample of healthy adults (n=22, ages 19–35). The paper reports whole-brain task contrasts (arm>baseline, palm>baseline, arm>palm) and presents results in text, figures, and tables, satisfying reporting requirements. Methods, results, and connectivity analyses are described in the full text. Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria (I3, I4, I5, I6) and violates no exclusion criteria. Full text appears complete.

This is an fMRI study of emotional prosody comprehension contrasting simple vs. complex (including social) emotions, which is a social-communication / perception-of-others task. Sample comprises healthy adult participants (n=19, ages 18–51). The paper reports whole-brain, group-level voxelwise analyses (SPM8 contrasts, corrected cluster-wise results) with tables of coordinates and figures. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Thus all inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, and I6 are satisfied and no exclusion criteria apply.

The study reports an fMRI experiment using a social-related task (minimal-group/team membership influencing action perception and judgments), satisfying I3. The sample comprises healthy adult volunteers (reported ages 17–43 for the fMRI group), and group-level results for the healthy sample are reported, satisfying I4 (note: a small number of participants are age 17, but the sample is otherwise healthy adults and results are reported at the group level). The paper reports whole-brain, group-level task activation analyses with cluster-level FWE correction and provides coordinates and Z-values (PFWE < 0.05 across whole-brain and tables/figures), satisfying I5 and I6. The full text (intro, methods, results, discussion) is present. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, patient-only, age-only outside range, or non-empirical) are triggered. Therefore the study meets all required inclusion criteria for this meta-analysis.

This is an empirical fMRI study using a social working memory task (social cognition) in healthy adult participants (n=16; mean age 20). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked analyses (parametric effects across load) with coordinates and references to Tables S2/S3 and surface-rendered maps, clearly from the healthy/control group. The methods, results, and discussion are present in the full text provided. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I3 (fMRI social task), I4 (healthy adult sample), I5 (whole-brain group-level voxelwise maps), and I6 (results reported in tables/figures). No exclusion criteria are met. Full text appears complete.

Meets all inclusion criteria: (I3) uses task-based fMRI of empathic/social decision-making; (I4) sample of healthy adults (N=32, mean age 22.8) reported separately; (I5) reports group-level whole-brain voxelwise task effects (GLM results, cluster-level correction) and tables of activations; (I6) whole-brain results are described in text/tables/figures. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, healthy adult group reported, empirical fMRI data present). Full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion so appears complete. Therefore INCLUDED for the review of fMRI studies of social processing in healthy adults.

This is an empirical fMRI study in healthy adults (N=20, mean age 22) that uses task-based fMRI to compare neural responses to communicative versus noncommunicative vocal sounds, which directly addresses social communication processing. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise contrasts (e.g., vocal > nonvocal; communicative > noncommunicative) thresholded with FDR and provides peak coordinates and whole-brain maps/figures, satisfying whole-brain reporting requirements. Methods, results, and discussion are present in the provided full text and no exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not between-groups-only, participants are within 18–65, and it is empirical). Therefore all inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, and I6 are met and no exclusion criteria are applicable.

This is an empirical fMRI study using BOLD fMRI while participants made pleasantness ratings of social images (affiliation, isolation) — satisfying the social-related task requirement. The sample includes a healthy younger adult group (mean age 20.75), meeting the 18–65 age criterion. The paper reports whole-brain, group-level voxelwise analyses (random-effects contrasts, conjunctions) with tables/figures and peak coordinates for healthy groups. Reporting of whole-brain results in tables/figures meets acceptable reporting formats. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not resting-state/seed-only, not exclusively outside age range, and is empirical). Full text appears complete (includes introduction, methods, results, discussion, and tables/figures). Therefore the study meets inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, and I6 and should be INCLUDED.

This paper reports an empirical fMRI study using a social cognitive task (Visual–Verbal Self-Other Referential Processing Task) probing self- and other-referential processing (social cognition). The sample comprises 20 healthy adult women aged 18–52 (within 18–65). Whole-brain, group-level voxelwise analyses are reported (SPM8 preprocessing, voxel-wise maps, cluster thresholds, group contrasts, Tables and Figures showing activation maps), fulfilling the requirement for whole-brain task-evoked maps for the healthy group. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity/rest-only, between-group-only contrasts, out-of-range ages, or non-empirical paper) are met. Full article content (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is present. Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria and should be included.

This is an event-related fMRI study of social evaluation (impression formation) using task-based fMRI contrasts. It includes a healthy young adult group (ages 20–29), satisfying the requirement for a healthy adult sample within 18–65. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses (conjunctions and contrasts) with corrected thresholds and tabulated/figure results described for the healthy groups. Full article content (intro, methods, results, discussion) is provided. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, age-only, non-empirical) apply.

This is an fMRI study of impression formation/updating (a social-cognitive task: perception and understanding of others) in healthy adults (N=24, ages 18–45). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain task-evoked analyses (interaction and L2>F3 contrasts), with voxel-wise thresholds, cluster correction, tables/figures, and supplemental figures—satisfying whole-brain reporting. Full article content (intro, methods, results, discussion) is provided. Therefore all required inclusion criteria are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study of affective speech comprehension that explicitly examines social-cognitive processes (theory-of-mind/mentalizing) during an emotional sentence classification task. The sample comprises 51 healthy adults (age range 18–53). Group-level, whole-brain task-evoked statistical maps and contrasts (EMO vs GRAM) are reported (SPM results, coordinates, figures), satisfying whole-brain evidence requirements. The provided full text includes introduction, methods (participants, tasks, imaging, analysis), results, and discussion; thus the full text appears complete. Therefore all inclusion criteria are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

The article reports an empirical fMRI study of social processing (empathy/threat to self, friend, stranger) in healthy adult participants (n=22, mean age 23.6). It includes whole-brain task-evoked analyses (threat minus safe contrasts), conjunction and voxelwise higher-level analyses with cluster-wise thresholds and reported coordinates/clusters (tables/figures and supplementary whole-brain results). The methods, results, and discussion are present in the full text. Therefore it satisfies inclusion criteria I3 (fMRI social-related task), I4 (healthy adult sample 18–65), I5 (group-level whole-brain task-evoked statistical maps reported), and I6 (whole-brain results reported with coordinates/figures). No exclusion criteria (E2–E6) apply. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This study uses task-based fMRI of social influence (adult expert advice) during decision making, and it includes a healthy adult group (ages 18–45), satisfying I3 and I4. However, the paper’s neuroimaging results focus on developmental (age-group) contrasts and report ROI/parametric analyses and group-comparison effects; it does not present a clearly identified whole-brain, group-level task activation map for the healthy adult group alone (i.e., an unmasked within-group voxelwise map for adults). Therefore it does not meet inclusion criterion I5 and must be excluded under E4 (reports mainly between-group/developmental contrasts without an accompanying whole-brain healthy-group task map). Inclusion criteria met: I3, I4. Inclusion criteria not met: I5 (whole-brain adult group map absent). Exclusion applied: E4. Full text appears complete.

The study meets all inclusion criteria: (I3) It uses fMRI during viewing of social/emotion-laden movie clips targeting perception/understanding of others, empathy, and social processing. (I4) Sample comprises healthy adults (n=16, ages 25–49). (I5) The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses (intersubject correlation maps, GLM maps relating valence/arousal to ISC) with statistical correction and figures/tables. (I6) Whole-brain results are presented in figures and supplemental tables and clearly described in the text. The provided full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion; therefore fulltext_incomplete is false.

This paper reports task-based fMRI in healthy adult participants (N=94 healthy right-handed women, age 18–35) using a social-affective task (Socio-affective Video Task) probing compassion/empathy/positive and negative affect, which is directly relevant to social processing (meets I3). The sample is a healthy adult group within the 18–65 range (meets I4). The manuscript reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task activation contrasts (e.g., HE vs LE; parametric modulations) with FWE-corrected results and tables/figures describing these effects (meets I5 and I6). The study is empirical and provides whole-brain task activation maps for the healthy group rather than ROI-only or connectivity-only results; no exclusion criteria apply. Full text appears complete with Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. Therefore the study should be INCLUDED for the meta-analysis.

This is an empirical fMRI study of social cognition (learning/simulating others' decisions) using a social prediction task (Other task). The paper reports data from healthy, normal adult participants (39 recruited; 36 analyzed) and provides whole-brain, group-level voxelwise task analyses (whole-brain regression results, cluster-corrected maps, Tables 1–2 and figures). Results are reported for the healthy participant group (within-group effects). The full text (introduction, methods, results, discussion, and tables/figures) is present. Therefore it satisfies the meta-analysis requirements for fMRI studies of social-related processing in healthy adults.

This is an empirical fMRI study presenting movie clips designed to elicit affiliation and power motives (a social-related task), scanned in healthy adult participants (N=17 male students, mean age 23.6). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain task contrasts (affiliation>control and power>control) analyzed with SPM5 and provides cluster results with MNI coordinates and figures/tables. Full article text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is present. Thus it meets inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, and I6 and violates no exclusion criteria. Full text appears complete for screening purposes.

This is an empirical fMRI study of social cognition in healthy adults: task involved viewing cooperative vs. affective social interactions during functional MRI (meets I3). Sample consisted of 27 healthy right-handed adult participants with ages in the adult range (means ~25–26), meeting I4. The paper reports group-level whole-brain voxelwise task contrasts and conjunctions (p<0.05 FWE and uncorrected maps), tables of activation foci and figures derived from healthy participants (meets I5 and I6). No exclusion criteria apply: whole-brain results are reported (not ROI-only), this is not resting-state/connectivity-only, results for healthy adults are separately reported, and it is an empirical study. Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion).

This fMRI study investigates social perception using naturalistic audiovisual movie clips in 19 healthy adults (ages 21–34). It uses task-based fMRI and reports group-level, whole-brain, voxelwise GLM results (contrasts, FDR-corrected maps) comparing social vs. non-social features and feature-specific effects; results are presented in figures/tables and described in the text. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria for the review (I3, I4, I5, I6) and violates no exclusion criteria. Full text appears complete for screening.

This is an empirical fMRI study of affiliative social processing in healthy adults (n=27 analyzed; ages within 18–65). The task explicitly probes affiliation/attachment via written social scenarios and uses functional MRI. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task contrasts (e.g., affiliative vs nonaffiliative; FWE-corrected results are reported and tabulated) from the healthy participant group. Full article text (Introduction, Methods, Results, Discussion) is provided. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5 and I6, and violates no exclusion criteria. The sample had some excluded participants for signal dropout, but healthy-group whole-brain results are clearly reported for the remaining sample.

This is an empirical fMRI study in adult participants (primiparous mothers, mean age 24.1) using a social/attachment-related task (listening to own infant cry vs other/control sounds). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked analyses (FEAT/FLAME) with cluster-level results and coordinates, and figures illustrating activations. All inclusion criteria are met: (I3) fMRI during a social/attachment task; (I4) sample includes healthy adult participants (none met current MDE at time of scanning); (I5) whole-brain, group-level task activation maps/results are reported; (I6) results are described in text and tables/figures. No exclusion criteria apply (no ROI-only, no connectivity-only or patient-only unreported healthy maps, age range appropriate, empirical data present). Full text appears complete (includes introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an empirical fMRI study of social cognition (empathy/perspective taking) using a task that instructs Self/Other/View perspective taking (meets I3). The sample is 18 healthy adults aged 21–31, reported separately (meets I4). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task contrasts and conjunction analyses with cluster- and peak-level FWE correction and tables of activations (meets I5 and I6). No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not between-group-only, participants are within 18–65, and it is empirical). Full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, Discussion, and tables/figures (fulltext_incomplete=false). Therefore include in the review.

This is an empirical fMRI study that includes explicit social-related tasks (social videos and texts probing understanding of others’ mental/emotional states). Participants are healthy adult volunteers (N=45; mean age 20.5). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task activation/deactivation contrasts (fixed and random effects, multiple-comparison correction; peak coordinates in Appendix A) and displays whole-brain statistical maps/figures (e.g., Figures 3–4). Thus it meets I3, I4, I5 and I6. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, includes within-group healthy task effects, participants within age range, empirical data present). Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion, appendices).

This article reports an event-related fMRI study of processing emotional facial expressions—a social communication / perception-of-others task—using healthy adult human participants (n=23, ages 24–34). The paper presents group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses (random-effects group analysis, cluster-wise correction) with significance maps and stereotactic coordinates, satisfying reporting requirements. All inclusion criteria are met (I3: social-related fMRI task; I4: healthy adult sample; I5: whole-brain group-level results reported; I6: results reported via maps and coordinates). No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity/resting-only, includes within-group whole-brain task effects, appropriate age range, and is empirical). Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion present).

This is an fMRI study of social cognition (action observation, mirror-neuron and mentalizing systems) in healthy adults (N=19, ages 18–32). The paper reports group-level, voxelwise task analyses (random-effects ANOVA) and explicitly states that whole-brain results are provided in the Supplemental Methods, satisfying the requirement that qualifying whole-brain results may appear in supplemental materials. The task is social-related (why/how action understanding), and healthy-group results are clearly described. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion (supplemental material noted but absence is acceptable). No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only, out-of-range ages, or non-empirical) are met. Therefore the study meets inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, and I6 and should be included.

This is an fMRI study of visual perspective taking/theory-of-mind (social cognition) in healthy adults. The sample comprises healthy adult participants (N=16, mean age 22.4). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task activation contrasts analyzed in SPM with cluster-level FWE correction and tables/figures of results (e.g., Inconsistent Other > Consistent Other; conjunctions), satisfying whole-brain reporting. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Therefore it meets all meta-analysis inclusion criteria for healthy adult fMRI studies of social processing.

This is an empirical fMRI study in healthy adults (N=21, mean age 24) that investigates action observation and mirror responses, a form of social-related processing (Perception and Understanding of Others). The study reports task-based fMRI with both ROI and whole-brain analyses (a whole-brain analysis is described at p<0.001 uncorrected with reported peak coordinates and rendered SPMs), providing group-level, voxelwise task-evoked results for the healthy participant sample. Full-text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I3 (social-related fMRI task), I4 (healthy adult sample 18–65), I5 (group-level whole-brain task maps), and I6 (whole-brain results reported in text/figures/tables). No exclusion criteria apply.

This is an empirical fMRI study of social cognition using task-based BOLD imaging while participants viewed ostensive vs. non-ostensive social stimuli (meets I3). The sample comprised 22 healthy adult volunteers (mean age 25) reported separately (meets I4). The authors performed group-level voxelwise analyses (two group RFX whole-brain ANOVAs) and report task-evoked group contrasts with peak coordinates and statistical inference (including exploratory whole-brain findings and ROI small-volume corrected results), which constitutes the required group-level whole-brain task-evoked reporting (meets I5 and I6). The full article text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is present and no exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only, out-of-range ages, or non-empirical) are met. Therefore the study is eligible for inclusion in the meta-analysis.

This paper reports an fMRI experiment manipulating sociality (trustworthiness) vs nonsocial information using an n-back task in healthy adults (mean age 22). It provides whole-brain, group-level voxelwise analyses (2×2 repeated-measures ANOVA) with cluster correction and tables of peak voxels for main effects and interaction, clearly reported for the healthy sample. Thus it meets inclusion criteria I3 (social-related fMRI task), I4 (healthy adult participants within 18–65), I5 (group-level whole-brain task-evoked maps), and I6 (results reported in tables/figures and described in text). No exclusion criteria apply. Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion present).

This paper reports an fMRI study in healthy adult participants (N≈36, ages ~21) using a social-related task (perception of others’ pain / empathy). The manuscript includes whole-brain, group-level task-evoked analyses (painful vs non-painful contrasts) with reported voxelwise results (tables/figures, FDR-corrected thresholds) clearly identified for the healthy/control sample. The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. Therefore it meets all required inclusion criteria and does not violate any exclusion criteria.

This empirical fMRI study examines person-related social processing (familiar vs. unfamiliar faces), meeting the review objective. Inclusion criteria met: I3 (task is social/person memory/familiarity), I4 (healthy adult sample: final N=15 females, mean age 22.3 within 18–65), I5 (reports whole-brain, group-level voxelwise task analyses using random-effects GLM and FDR-corrected maps), and I6 (whole-brain results reported with coordinates and tables). No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity/resting-state only, not between-group-only contrasts, ages within range, and is an empirical fMRI study). The provided full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion; fulltext appears complete.

The study uses task-based fMRI to probe perception of others (gender perception of faces), which fits the social-related constructs (I3). The sample comprises healthy adult participants (ages 19–42; N=15 analyzed), meeting the sample criterion (I4). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain random-effects voxelwise analyses (contrast gender-different > gender-same) with statistical thresholds and cluster correction, and it describes/report coordinates and figures of resulting clusters (right collateral sulcus, left precuneus, right lateral occipital gyrus, right putamen), satisfying whole-brain evidence requirements (I5,I6). The full text provided contains Introduction, Methods, Results, Discussion, and References (fulltext_incomplete=false). No exclusion criteria apply. Therefore the study should be INCLUDED.

This is an empirical fMRI study using a social task contrasting human vs computer opponents (social-related processing). Participants are healthy adults (final N=17; mean age 23.5), within the 18–65 range. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain random-effects analyses and presents voxelwise contrasts (Conflict > No Conflict; Condition × Conflict interaction) with thresholding and tables/figures of activations and coordinates. Full article text (Introduction, Methods, Results, Discussion) is provided. Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria and does not meet any exclusion criteria.

This is an empirical fMRI study in healthy adults (N=24, ages 18–27) that used task-based whole-brain analyses. The tasks probe social-cognitive processes (Why-How paradigm asking about why/how people perform actions and Category-Exemplar items that engage representation of others/objects), implicating mentalizing and social perception networks. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise contrasts (e.g., How>Why, Why>How, Exemplars>Categories, Categories>Exemplars), conjunction analyses, and tables/figures with region coordinates and corrected thresholds. No exclusion criteria apply: it is not ROI-only, not connectivity- or resting-state-only, includes healthy adult participants within 18–65, and is an original empirical report. Full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion, so the provided full text appears complete. Therefore the study meets inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, and I6 and none of the exclusion criteria.

This is an empirical fMRI study of social-related processing (comparisons of physical attractiveness), using a task that assesses perception/understanding of others (beauty judgments). Sample consists of 25 healthy adult women (mean age 23.5), within the 18–65 range. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses with statistical maps, thresholding, conjunctions, and coordinate tables (whole-brain results reported and described). The full text (intro, methods, results, discussion) is present. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, outside age range, non-empirical) are met.

This is an empirical fMRI study of social processing in healthy adults. It used fMRI to decode learned social roles (social-affiliation/interaction) via a pre- and post-learning face perception task (I3). The sample comprised 15 healthy adults aged ~24 years, meeting the age/sample criterion (I4). The paper reports a group-level, whole-brain searchlight analysis with results corrected for multiple comparisons and peak MNI coordinates in superior temporal sulcus (i.e., whole-brain voxelwise group results), satisfying whole-brain evidence requirements (I5). Whole-brain results are described in text and reported with coordinates (I6). The full text provided contains Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion and appears complete. No exclusion criteria apply (no ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only, out-of-range ages, or non-empirical paper). Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria and should be INCLUDED.

This is an empirical fMRI study of social cognition (mentalizing about groups vs. individuals) using task-based functional MRI. Participants are healthy adults (ages 18–27 across experiments) meeting the sample criterion. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain, voxelwise task contrasts (e.g., group mental > group physical, member mental > member physical, individual mental > individual physical) with voxel-wise thresholds, cluster extent corrections, tables of identified regions/coordinates, figures, and corrected experiment-wide significance — satisfying whole-brain evidence and acceptable reporting formats. The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion (Experiments 1 & 2), so the full text is complete. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity/resting-state only, not between-group-only contrasts, participants within age range, and it is empirical). Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria for the review.

This is an empirical fMRI study of social processing (romantic interest/rejection) using a task that involves social affiliation/understanding. Scanned sample includes healthy adult participants (N=38; ages 19–31) with screening for psychiatric diagnoses. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task contrasts (e.g., Match vs Unrequited, violations of expectations) thresholded and reported with tables of peak coordinates and cluster-level correction; figures and detailed methods/results are present. Therefore it meets the meta-analysis requirements for fMRI social tasks, healthy adult sample, and whole-brain evidence. The full text provided includes Introduction, Methods, Results, Discussion, tables, and references and appears complete for screening.

This is an empirical fMRI study (task-based) on social communication/intent understanding (communicative vs private intentions), using healthy adult participants (N=23, mean age ~24). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task contrasts (e.g., CInt > PInt; interaction effects) with stereotaxic coordinates and statistical thresholds, and additional PPI analyses. Whole-brain results are clearly described in text, tables, and figures. All required inclusion criteria (I3, I4, I5, I6) are satisfied. No exclusion criteria apply: results are not ROI-only, not limited to connectivity-only, not only between-group contrasts, and participants are within 18–65. Full text appears complete (includes introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an empirical fMRI study of social-related processing (handholding during threat) in healthy adults (N=22, mean age 23.6). The task explicitly probes affiliation/attachment-related regulation (friend vs stranger vs alone) using BOLD fMRI. The paper reports group-level whole-brain analyses (cluster-wise FEAT/FLAME contrasts, ROIs derived from group threat>safe contrasts) and presents ROI coordinates and cluster statistics (Table 1), meeting the requirement for whole-brain task-evoked results reported for the healthy group. The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only, out-of-range ages, or non-empirical) are met.

This is an empirical fMRI study in healthy adults (n=18, mean age 26) that used tasks probing social communication (explicit laughter type categorization and implicit bout counting) addressing perception and understanding of others. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain second-level random-effects analyses (voxelwise contrasts, cluster-level FWE correction) with coordinates, figures and tables of results, and additionally supplementary whole-brain PPI connectivity analyses. All inclusion criteria are met: I3 (fMRI during social-related task), I4 (healthy adult sample 18–65), I5 (group-level whole-brain task-evoked voxelwise maps reported), and I6 (results presented in text/tables/figures). No exclusion criteria apply. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an fMRI study of social communicative gesture processing and imitation in healthy adults. It reports task-based whole-brain group-level voxelwise analyses (flexible factorial ANOVA) with voxel coordinates, cluster-correction (Monte Carlo), and multiple contrasts (e.g., IMI>CT, S>NS, interactions), clearly derived from the healthy participant group (data from 20 healthy adults, mean age 24.6). The task probes social communication/mentalizing and self/other processing, matching the review objective. Full article content (introduction, methods, results, discussion, references) is provided. No exclusion criteria are met.

This study meets all inclusion criteria for the review objective. It uses task-based fMRI during a social-related task (perception/understanding of others’ suffering; I3). The sample is healthy adults within the 18–65 range (mean ages ~22; I4). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses (e.g., Group × Redistribution Rank interaction; whole-brain corrected results identifying IPC and DLPFC; conjunction and PPI analyses reported with whole-brain or ROI corrections), satisfying the requirement for whole-brain task-evoked statistical maps originating from the healthy groups (I5). Results and statistical maps are described in the text and supplemental tables/figures (I6). Full text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is present in the provided content. No exclusion criteria are met. Therefore the study should be INCLUDED.

This is an empirical fMRI study that directly investigates social-related processing (reward for self vs friend vs antagonist) using a task involving social relationships and reward. The sample comprises healthy adults (N=31; ages 18–26), satisfying the adult healthy sample requirement. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain task-evoked analyses (repeated-measures ANOVAs) with voxelwise results, tables of coordinates, figures, and small-volume corrected findings clearly attributed to the healthy group. Core article content (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is present. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only, out-of-range ages, or non-empirical) are met.

This is an empirical fMRI study that examines social communication/mentalizing processes (message propagation, influencer perspective) during an in-scanner task, satisfying the review’s social-related task requirement. The fMRI sample comprises healthy adult interns (N=19; mean age 20.55), within the 18–65 range. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain random-effects analyses (thresholds, MNI coordinates, Table 1, figures) rather than ROI-only or connectivity-only results. The provided full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion, allowing verification of criteria. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only, wrong age range, or non-empirical) apply. Therefore the study meets inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, and I6 and is eligible for inclusion in the meta-analysis.

This paper reports an fMRI task investigating recognition of others’ ‘vitality forms’ (social perception/understanding of others), using task-based whole-brain analyses. Sample: 19 healthy adults (ages 21–29) are reported separately. Group-level, whole-brain voxelwise contrasts (e.g., how vs what) are described with coordinates and PFWE thresholds in tables and figures. Whole-brain results are clearly identified for the healthy/control group. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Therefore it meets I3 (social-related fMRI task), I4 (healthy adult sample 18–65), I5 (group-level whole-brain task-evoked maps reported), and I6 (results reported as coordinates/figures). No exclusion criteria apply. Full text appears complete.

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study investigating theory-of-mind/emotion/pain processing (social cognition) in healthy adult participants (N=46, ages 18–31). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise second-level analyses (univariate contrasts and MVPA), with tables/figures and detailed methods/results/discussion. Whole-brain results are clearly attributed to the healthy/control group and reported in text, figures, and tables. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion, so appears complete. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, and I6, and violates no exclusion criteria.

This study used fMRI during a social-evaluation task in a sample of healthy participants that included adults (ages 18–22.9), so it meets I3 (fMRI social-related task) and I4 (contains healthy adult participants). However, the paper reports whole-brain, group-level analyses focused on age effects across a mixed-age sample (children, adolescents, young adults) and reports age-related/interaction maps rather than an unmasked, whole-brain task-evoked activation map clearly identified as coming from an adult-only healthy group. Therefore it does not meet I5 (a whole-brain, group-level task map clearly identified as coming from the healthy adult group). This corresponds to exclusion criterion E4 (reports only interactions/age effects without an accompanying unmasked, whole-brain healthy-group task effect). Full text appears complete (supplemental materials referenced but not required).

This is an empirical fMRI study of social perception using a social-related task (perception of nonverbal dyadic interactions) in healthy adults (21 right-handed male participants, ages 23–33). The paper reports whole-brain, group-level voxelwise task activation analyses (SPM8, flexible factorial ANOVA) with contrasts and cluster-corrected results and coordinates described in tables and figures. The methods, results, and discussion are complete in the provided full text. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not resting-state/connectivity-only, not between-group-only, participants within 18–65, and this is empirical fMRI data). Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria and should be included in the meta-analysis.

This is an fMRI study of social impression formation in healthy adult participants (N=19, mean age 19.1). The task is social (forming impressions of real people; outcome-dependency manipulation) and BOLD fMRI was acquired. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain random-effects GLM contrasts (e.g., functional localizer contrast form-impression > sequencing) with cluster-corrected results and Talairach coordinates (Table 1) and main-task coordinates (Table 2), satisfying whole-brain reporting requirements. Results are described for the healthy participant group. Full article text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is present. Therefore inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5 and I6 are met; no exclusion criteria apply.

This paper reports an fMRI study of social perception (passive viewing of biological vs. scrambled point-light displays), satisfying the review’s social-task requirement. It includes a healthy adult sample (n=48, ages 20–35) with results for the healthy adult group reported separately. Group-level, whole-brain, voxelwise task-evoked analyses are reported (main effect biological>scrambled; Sex×Condition ANOVA) with cluster correction and coordinate tables/figures. Whole-brain results are clearly described in text, tables, and figures. Therefore inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, and I6 are met. No exclusion criteria (E2–E6) apply. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study in healthy adults (ages 19–28) investigating social-signal processing (eye-gaze and self-propelled motion) and its link to mental-state inference. Group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses are reported (second-level one-sample t-tests, voxel-by-voxel regression, cluster correction, coordinates/figures/tables of activation peaks are provided). The sample includes a healthy adult group and results are reported for that group. Therefore it satisfies inclusion criteria I3 (fMRI during social-related tasks), I4 (healthy adult sample reported separately), I5 (group-level whole-brain task-evoked maps), and I6 (whole-brain results reported in figures/tables/text). No exclusion criteria (E2–E6) are met. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This fMRI study uses a social-cognition task (third-party punishment; mentalizing and moral judgment) addressing perception/understanding of others, meeting I3. The sample is 26 healthy adults (age ~26), within 18–65, meeting I4. The paper reports whole-brain, group-level random-effects GLM results with FDR thresholding and Talairach coordinates (R TPJ, R AI) and presents main effects and interactions clearly for the healthy group, satisfying I5 and I6. The full text provided includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion, so fulltext appears complete. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, non-healthy-only, age-out-of-range, or non-empirical) are met. Therefore the study should be INCLUDED.

This is an empirical fMRI study in healthy adult participants (male drivers aged 19–30) using a social-related task (viewing traffic awareness campaign videos that elicit mentalizing/empathy). The paper reports group-level task contrasts (CV vs NV) and presents whole-brain analyses for each group (Fig.1 and associated description), including results identified for the safe driver (control) group, satisfying the requirement for a healthy-group whole-brain task activation map. Methods, results, and discussion are present in the full text. No exclusion criteria are met.

This is an FMRI study of face perception (a social-related task) in a healthy sample that includes an adult subgroup, so I3 and I4 are satisfied. However, the paper does not report a group-level, whole-brain task-evoked statistical map that is clearly identified as coming from the healthy adult subgroup (18–65) — the whole-brain results are presented as age-regression across the full healthy sample (children through adults) rather than an adult-only within-group activation map. Because the meta-analysis requires at least one whole-brain healthy-adult group task map (I5), I5 is not met. No exclusion criteria from the list are explicitly triggered. Therefore the study must be excluded for failure to meet I5 (adult-specific whole-brain task activation map).

This is an empirical fMRI study of social processing (attribute framing/self and reflected perspectives) using healthy adult participants (ages 19–41). The methods describe voxelwise whole-brain GLM analyses and report group-level whole-brain contrasts with coordinates and cluster thresholds (e.g., positive minus negative frame, frame-inconsistent minus frame-consistent), satisfying the requirement for whole-brain task-evoked maps. Behavioral and neuroimaging results are reported for the healthy sample. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not between-group-only, participants within 18–65, and it is empirical). Therefore all required inclusion criteria are met and the study should be INCLUDED.

Available content is limited to the abstract, metadata, and references; the full article text (methods, participants, detailed results/tables) is not accessible. Inclusion: I3 is satisfied — the study used fMRI during a social-related task (approachability judgments of faces). Inclusion I4 (healthy adult sample 18–65) cannot be confirmed because participant age and sample details are not provided in the accessible content. Inclusion I5 (reporting of at least one group-level whole-brain voxelwise task activation map for the healthy/control group) cannot be confirmed: the abstract reports activations but does not explicitly state whole-brain, voxelwise, group-level maps or provide coordinates/tables. Because the full text is incomplete, key inclusion criteria cannot be verified. No explicit exclusion criteria (E2–E6) can be confidently applied based on the truncated content, so exclusion is due to inability to verify required inclusion criteria from the incomplete full text.

The article reports task-based fMRI in healthy adult participants performing a social-empathy paradigm (empathic judgments), with two independent group-level whole-brain analyses (fMRI1 exploratory whole-brain uncorrected; fMRI2 group analyses with SVC and additional whole-brain testing) and voxelwise task-evoked contrasts reported with coordinates and figures. Sample consists of healthy adult subjects (female undergraduates). The paper includes full methods, results, and discussion. Thus it meets inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, and I6; no exclusion criteria apply.

Although this is an fMRI task of social processing with group-level whole-brain results, the participant sample includes individuals younger than 18 (age range 16.9–25.7) and the paper does not report a separate healthy-adult subgroup (18–65) analysis. Therefore it does not clearly meet the sample criterion (I4). Inclusion criteria met: I3 (fMRI during a social-related task), I5 (group-level whole-brain task-evoked results reported), I6 (whole-brain results clearly described/tabled). Inclusion criterion not met: I4 (healthy adult group 18–65 not clearly satisfied because sample includes minors and no adult-only subgroup analysis is reported). No exclusion criteria (E2–E6) are directly triggered; full text appears complete.

This is an fMRI study of social processing (collaboration vs competition) using a social incentive force task, meeting the review objective. Participants were healthy adults (N=32, ages 18–39). The paper reports whole-brain, group-level voxelwise task-evoked analyses (SPM GLM, clusterwise FWE correction) with reported activation maps and coordinates (basal ganglia, TPJ, mPFC) and VBM structural results. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, non-empirical, or out-of-range samples) apply.

This is an empirical fMRI study in healthy adult participants (n=20, ages 23–39) that examines social judgments (perception/understanding of others) using task-evoked functional MRI. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain (random-effects) voxelwise analyses (ANOVA and pairwise contrasts) with FDR-corrected results, statistical maps and tables of activations for the healthy sample. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion, and healthy-group whole-brain task effects are clearly identified. Therefore all inclusion criteria are met and no exclusion criteria are triggered.

This paper does not meet the meta-analysis requirements for inclusion. Although it examines social-related processing using the value-related moral sentiment task (VMST) in healthy adults (I4 met: N=63, mean age 28.1), the study does not use task-based functional MRI as part of its reported analyses (primary data are voxel-based morphometry/structural MRI). While the authors reference a prior fMRI study and use SSC-BOLD responses from a subgroup (N=29) as an explanatory variable, this paper does not report any group-level, whole-brain, task-evoked fMRI statistical maps for the healthy/control group (I3 NOT met; I5 NOT met). I6 is not applicable because no qualifying whole-brain fMRI results are presented. No exclusion criteria (E2–E6) specifically apply. Therefore the study must be excluded for failing to provide in-paper whole-brain task-evoked fMRI results in healthy adults.

This study reports original fMRI data collected during a live verbal social interaction (hyperscanning) involving healthy adult participants (22 right-handed women, mean age 27.2). The task is clearly social communication (speaking/listening about autobiographical events). Group-level voxelwise whole-brain analyses are reported (second-level t-tests, cluster thresholds, tables/figures) for talking, listening, and imagining conditions, satisfying whole-brain reporting requirements. No exclusion criteria apply: results are not limited to ROIs, are not solely connectivity/resting-state analyses, include a healthy adult sample within 18–65, and are empirical. Full text appears complete with methods, results, and discussion. Therefore the study meets inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, and I6 and should be INCLUDED in the meta-analysis.

This paper reports an fMRI task study of social processing (explicit judgments of trustworthiness and attractiveness from voices), in healthy adult participants (N=44, ages 21–60). The methods include whole-brain, voxelwise group-level analyses with corrected cluster-level inference and reported MNI coordinates (tables/figures), clearly from the healthy group. The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. Thus it satisfies inclusion criteria I3 (fMRI during social-related task), I4 (healthy adult sample 18–65), I5 (whole-brain group-level task activation maps reported), and I6 (results reported in tables/figures/text). No exclusion criteria are met. Full text appears complete for screening (not truncated).

This is an empirical fMRI study of social communication/empathy using naturalistic video stimuli (meets I3). The sample comprises 27 healthy adult participants (mean age 34.07; meets I4). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain random-effects GLM results and voxelwise contrasts/conjunctions (including figures and MNI coordinates), satisfying whole-brain evidence requirements (meets I5 and I6). The full text (introduction, methods, results, discussion, and supplementary references) is present and complete. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not between-group-only, healthy adult group reported, and empirical). Therefore the study should be INCLUDED.

This is an fMRI study of social cognition (empathy, Theory of Mind, self–other differentiation) using task-based whole-brain BOLD contrasts in healthy adult participants aged 18–40. Methods describe whole-brain random-effects analyses with voxelwise thresholds and cluster extent correction; results report group-level whole-brain contrasts, coordinates, conjunctions, and condition effects for the healthy group. The sample is healthy adults (N=15) and results are reported for that group. The paper is empirical and includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion, so full text appears complete. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, and I6 and none of the exclusion criteria apply.

This is an fMRI study of social decision-making (one-shot Prisoner’s Dilemma), investigating social value orientation and trust—clearly a social-related task. Participants are healthy adults (N=35 analyzed; mean age 24.6, within 18–65). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked analyses (GLM contrasts, cluster-size correction, reported coordinates, tables and figures of activation maps), satisfying whole-brain evidence reporting. The full text includes introduction, methods (participants, image acquisition, preprocessing, GLM), results, figures/tables, and discussion. No exclusion criteria are met. Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria and should be INCLUDED.

This publication is a narrative review article (in Japanese) summarizing social neuroscience and fMRI findings rather than reporting original empirical fMRI data in healthy adults. The provided content is limited to abstract/metadata (full text not available here). Therefore it meets exclusion criterion E6 (non-empirical paper without original fMRI data). Inclusion criteria are not satisfied: I3 (the study itself does not use fMRI in an original experiment), I4 (no original healthy adult sample reported), I5 (no group-level whole-brain task-evoked statistical maps from a healthy group), and I6 (no qualifying whole-brain results reported). Because only abstract/metadata are provided, fulltext_incomplete=true.

This paper reports an fMRI study of social-related processing (familiar/partner face perception; social cognition: perception and understanding of others), includes a healthy control group of adults (13 healthy volunteers, mean age 64.5), and presents group-level, whole-brain, voxelwise task-evoked contrasts for the control group (e.g., partner > unfamiliar faces) with peak coordinates and cluster-level corrected results. Whole-brain results are reported in text/tables/figures (satisfies I6). The full text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is provided. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only, non-empirical, or exclusively out-of-range participants) are met. Therefore the study meets inclusion criteria I3, I5, and I6; the healthy control sample meets I4 as a group of healthy adults reported separately. Full text appears complete.

This is an empirical fMRI study using the ultimatum game (a social decision-making task) and reports group-level whole-brain task contrasts. The sample includes a healthy adult group (n=15; ages 19–28) reported separately. The paper presents second-level, voxelwise analyses (unfair–fair contrasts), thresholded maps, post-hoc t-tests, and tables/figures describing activations for the healthy groups, satisfying whole-brain reporting requirements. The full text (intro, methods, results, discussion, references) is provided. Therefore the study meets inclusion criteria for fMRI social-task data in healthy adults and does not meet any exclusion criteria.

This is an fMRI study of online social interaction (free reciprocal imitation) in healthy adult participants (N=23, females aged 18–30). The paper reports group-level whole-brain GLM activation contrasts (e.g., imitating vs rest, being imitated vs rest, observation vs rest) with familywise error correction and provides coordinates/tables and figures. Although the paper also reports PPI connectivity analyses, it clearly includes unmasked whole-brain task-evoked activation maps from the healthy group. Full text (Introduction, Methods, Results, Discussion, References) is present. Thus inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5 and I6 are satisfied and no exclusion criteria apply.

This study used fMRI of natural touch by another person (a social-related task) in a sample of healthy adults, meeting inclusion criteria I3 and I4. However, the primary analyses are group-level ICA spatial maps and component time courses derived from task runs; the paper does not report a traditional group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task activation map or mass-univariate contrasts (e.g., t-maps/GLM contrasts) for the healthy group. Per exclusion criterion E3 (reports only ICA/connectivity-type analyses without a healthy-group whole-brain task activation map), the study must be excluded. Inclusion criteria met: I3, I4. Inclusion criteria not met: I5 (no group-level whole-brain task-evoked voxelwise map).

This is an empirical fMRI study of face perception (faces vs houses) addressing social-related processing (face perception/social cognition). Sample consists of healthy adult undergraduates (N=57, mean age 18.87) within 18–65 with no psychiatric diagnoses. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain second-level SPM analyses (significant activation clusters, Table 2, FWE-corrected maps and voxel counts in bilateral fusiform gyrus as suprathreshold voxels), and figures showing group activations; whole-brain voxelwise results are clearly described. All required inclusion criteria (I3, I4, I5, I6) are met. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity/resting-state-only, not between-group-only, age in range, empirical data present). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion present).

This is an fMRI study that includes a social-related task (social distance trials with participants' friends vs acquaintances) and reports results from healthy adult participants (N=15, ages 20–28). The paper presents group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses (searchlight MVPA and RSA) with FDR-corrected clusters and figures/tables identifying significant regions (e.g., right IPL), satisfying whole-brain reporting requirements. The full text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is provided. Therefore all inclusion criteria are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

The study meets I3 (uses task-based fMRI during a social closeness task) and I4 (sample includes healthy adult participants aged 19–30). However, it does NOT report any group-level, whole-brain (voxelwise) task activation maps for the healthy group; the fMRI analyses are restricted to predefined anatomical ROIs with extracted beta weights and SVC. Therefore it violates exclusion criterion E2 (ROI-only analyses with no whole-brain results). Because I5 (whole-brain evidence) is not satisfied, the study must be excluded.

This is an fMRI study of social self-processing (direct and reflected self-evaluations from peers) that clearly falls within social-related processing constructs (Perception/Understanding of Self and Others). The sample includes a healthy adult group (N=19; ages 22–31) reported separately alongside adolescents. The paper reports whole-brain, voxelwise group-level analyses (2×4×3 repeated-measures ANOVA) with corrected voxelwise and cluster thresholds and displays main effects and interaction maps (figures/tables). Separate age-group analyses are indicated (with supplementary materials referenced) and whole-brain ROI and voxelwise results are reported, satisfying the requirement that healthy-group whole-brain task effects are available (including tables/figures/supplement). Full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, Discussion. Therefore all inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, and I6 are met; no exclusion criteria apply.

This is an empirical fMRI study of social processing (bystander effect: observing emergencies with varying group sizes) meeting all inclusion criteria. I3: Task is social-related (perception/understanding of others) using movies of emergencies. I4: Sample consists of healthy adults aged 18–27 (group results reported). I5: Group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked analyses are reported (random-effects GLM, parametric maps, cluster-corrected results; tables/figures of coordinates/clusters). I6: Whole-brain results are reported in text/tables/figures. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not between-group-only, ages within range, empirical data present). Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion present).

The study is an empirical fMRI investigation of social cognitive processing (causal attribution/mentalizing), meeting the review objective. Inclusion criteria met: I3 (task-based fMRI during social/mentalizing task), I4 (healthy adult sample, ages 18–41, N=20, results reported for this group), I5 (reports group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses and whole-brain FWE-corrected results; Table 1 and conjunction/contrast whole-brain analyses described), and I6 (whole-brain results clearly described and reported). No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity/resting-only, not between-group-only, ages within range, empirical data present). Full text appears complete (includes introduction, methods, results, discussion, and conclusions). Thus the study should be INCLUDED.

The study reports an fMRI experiment using a social attribution task (attributing awareness to a cartoon face) in healthy adult participants (n=50, ages 18–49) and later a TMS follow-up. Group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task contrasts are reported (H trials − E trials) with corrected thresholds, cluster sizes, coordinates in Table 1, and figures showing surface maps and time series. Full methods, results, and discussion are provided. Thus it meets inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, and I6 and violates no exclusion criteria.

This is an fMRI study using social tasks (Cyberball exclusion and a modified Dictator Game) probing social processes (punishment and forgiveness), meeting I3. Sample comprises healthy adults (n=26, mean age 20.7), meeting I4. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task contrasts with peak coordinates and tables (e.g., Exclusion no ball > Inclusion ball; Excluders > Includers; Excluders equality > Includers equality), satisfying I5 and I6. The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion (not truncated), so fulltext_incomplete=false. No exclusion criteria (E2–E6) apply: analyses include whole-brain results (not ROI-only), not limited to connectivity-only or between-group-only contrasts, participants are within 18–65, and the paper is empirical. Therefore include.

This is an empirical fMRI study of social-related processing (anticipatory active interpersonal touch) in healthy adult participants (N=16, ages 20–34). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxel-wise task contrasts (multiple Target and Target×Modality contrasts), cluster-corrected statistical maps, conjunctions, and a tactile localizer; results are presented in figures/tables and described for the healthy group. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. No exclusion criteria apply: it is not ROI-only, not connectivity/resting-only, not between-group only, participants are within 18–65, and it is an empirical report. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, and I6 and should be included.

This paper reports an empirical fMRI study of self/other social-cognitive processing (conceptual and agentic self-referential recollection) in healthy adults (N=18; age range 19–29). Group-level, voxelwise whole-brain task activation analyses are reported (SPM8 second-level analyses with whole-brain FWE-corrected results and coordinate tables), and results are clearly identified as coming from the healthy/control group. The full text (introduction, methods, results, discussion, tables/figures description) is present and sufficient for screening. Therefore all inclusion criteria (I3, I4, I5, I6) are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

This is an empirical fMRI study of social processing: participants performed a competitive (intergroup vs individual) task during fMRI with self-referential/moral stimuli, addressing perception/understanding of self in social context. Sample: healthy adult volunteers (final N=21, Mage=23.1) within 18–65. The paper reports whole-brain, group-level random-effects analyses with corrected thresholds and provides whole-brain results/tables (Table 2) and coordinates; ROI analyses are also used but whole-brain maps are reported. Full article text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. Therefore it satisfies inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, and I6 and violates no exclusion criteria. Full text appears complete.

This fMRI study investigates facial color processing, a form of social communication/perception of others (social-related processing). It recruited 25 healthy adult participants (mean age 25.2), satisfying sample criteria. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise contrasts (natural-colored faces vs natural-colored scrambled images) used to localize face-selective regions and presents group-level activation maps and coordinates, fulfilling the whole-brain evidence requirement. Methods, results, and discussion are present in the provided full text. Therefore all applicable inclusion criteria are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

This paper reports original fMRI data during a social feedback task (social-related processing of self/other trait feedback), tested in healthy adult German and Chinese participants. Methods describe whole-brain SPM8 GLM analyses and report group-level, voxelwise task-evoked activation maps and corrected clusters (FWE-corrected results, tables and figures) for healthy groups.
